nodes.label: Academic calendar, syllabus, assessments and exams
academic_terms capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. With it off, or before any term is saved, timetables, close-day and attendance behave exactly as they do today, so the calendar is an optional overlay rather than a change to the core.

nodes.label: Academic term
nodes.rationale: A term is a stretch of one academic year. kind is teaching, exam, break or internship. Dates are inclusive and must sit inside the academic year. A null semester means the whole year and overlaps every semester term. An exam, break or internship term wins over a teaching term on the same date. A date in no term is not a teaching day once the institution has any term.

nodes.label: teaching_weeks
nodes.rationale: Derived week list, one row per teaching term and Monday, with the teaching days left after closed terms and holidays. There is no view. services/academic_calendar.py is the only reader.

nodes.label: Teaching-day scheduling and cancellation
nodes.rationale: The greedy generator and the joint solver place sessions only on teaching days; a week with none fails. Close-day does not open a not_marked session on a non-teaching day, so the nightly digest skips exam and break days. Saving a term cancels unmarked sessions in an exam, break or internship term with cancel_reason calendar; sessions that already have marks are left, and deleting a term does not restore them. Marking a non-teaching day is refused unless that session was already held. Attendance percentages stay unchanged because a cancelled session was already outside the denominator. Holidays in institution_holidays are still removed on top.

nodes.label: syllabus capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. With it off the mark screen has no topic field, a topic sent by the mobile app is ignored, and nothing is written to lesson_logs. syllabus_units is the plan for one subject; lesson_logs is one topic per held lecture, with hours from 0.5 to 3 defaulting to 1. An invalid topic rejects that event before the mark is stored.

nodes.label: Syllabus coverage pace
nodes.rationale: Coverage is delivered hours of held lectures divided by planned hours. When the academic calendar is configured, expected hours are planned times elapsed teaching weeks over total teaching weeks; a week counts once its Monday is today or earlier. More than half an hour above that is ahead, more than half an hour below is behind, otherwise on_track. With no calendar the pace is no_pace and the percentage is still shown. Attendance percentages are unchanged.

nodes.label: assessments capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. With it off there is no Internals entry, the student and teacher tabs stay hidden, and nothing is stored. External results, grades and transcripts are not computed here. Students see a mark only after the component is locked; unlocking hides it again. Attainment figures and the report count every entered mark, locked or not.

nodes.label: Course and program outcome attainment
nodes.rationale: A component percentage is marks over maximum times 100. A course-outcome score is the weighted mean of the mapped component percentages; a weight of 0 on every mapped component counts them equally. Students with no mark on those components are left out. Attainment is the mean of the counted students. The level follows the share at or above 60 percent: 3 at 70 percent or more, 2 at 60, 1 at 50, otherwise 0. A program outcome is the mean of mapped course-outcome percentages weighted by correlation level 1 to 3, then the same bands.

nodes.label: exams capability
nodes.rationale: Off by default. With it off there is no Exams entry and nothing is stored. Room bookings and the weekly generator are otherwise unchanged. While bookings is on, solved rooms are busy at that date and time, so a new booking is refused and the generator avoids them for that week. A weekly timetable slot is not blocked by a one-day exam. Regular classes during an exam term are cancelled by the academic calendar when that capability is on, with reason calendar.

nodes.label: Exam seating and invigilation solver
nodes.rationale: Solving places every selected paper on one slot. Two papers that share a student never share a slot. A shared elective is one paper, so every cohort that selected it sits it together. Usable seats are room capacity divided by one more than the seating gap, then capped by students per room. Each used room gets one invigilator who is not absent, not unavailable, and not already on duty in that slot. Duties are spread so the busiest person has as few sessions as possible.
